claims.explanation: Norethindrone acetate is a progesterone receptor (PGR) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative/killing effect is most plausibly driven by PGR expression: lines that express the receptor respond to progestin-mediated growth inhibition and apoptosis, whereas PGR-negative or low-PGR lines are unaffected. The pattern of sensitive lines (endometrial/uterine, breast, some melanoma and sarcoma lines) and resistant lines (many lung, esophageal, and PGR-low tumors) is consistent with receptor-dependent activity rather than a specific co-mutation. TP53 mutation is common in both groups and is therefore not a strong selectivity driver, though loss of p53 may modulate downstream apoptotic response.

features.basis: Drug is a PGR agonist; receptor expression is required for progestin-mediated growth inhibition (PMID 16157482, 20943809)
TP53-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting impaired DNA-damage/apoptotic checkpoints that enhance progestin-induced death
Estrogen receptor-positive, hormone-dependent tumors often co-express PGR and are more responsive to hormonal therapy
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling and is common in sensitive endometrial, breast, and thyroid lines, potentially increasing dependence on hormonal growth signals
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven tumors may be more responsive to progestin-mediated inhibition
KRAS-mutant lines are present among sensitive colorectal, pancreatic, and gastric lines, possibly reflecting MAPK pathway dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling and is seen in several sensitive lines (melanoma, thyroid, glioma)
ARID1A mutations occur in sensitive endometrial, gastric, and bladder lines and may alter chromatin-dependent hormone receptor signaling
KMT2D mutations are frequent in sensitive lines and may affect enhancer-mediated PGR target gene expression
EGFR-mutant lung lines are predominantly in the least-affected group, suggesting EGFR-driven proliferation bypasses progestin growth inhibition
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may uncouple cell-cycle arrest from progestin signaling
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among resistant lines, suggesting constitutive PI3K activation reduces dependence on hormonal control
